moat_against: Partner concentration — a few large carriers/retailers/lenders control distribution and can rebid, squeeze, or move programs to Asurion/Likewize/in-house
No owned consumer brand or direct relationship — the end customer is the partner's
Lender-placed insurance is politically/regulatorily exposed and countercyclical to mortgage health
Global Housing catastrophe tail — earnings swing with cat load and reserve development
ROE only mid-teens with a 6.5% year (2022) — no wide-moat pricing power in the record
moat_for: Embedded distribution — multi-year programs inside carrier, retailer, auto-dealer and lender channels with systems integrated into point of sale and claims flow
Scale repair / trade-in / claims platform in Connected Living (Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA +29% YoY on new and expanded programs)
Leading lender-placed position — automatic placement when coverage lapses; countercyclical captive demand with inflation-guard pricing
Growing fee-based mix (fees and other income +19.6% YoY in Q2 2026), less cat-exposed than underwriting
moat_justification: Embedded B2B2C partnerships and program-integration switching costs in device protection and lender-placed insurance, but partners are large, concentrated and can rebid or in-source, there is no direct consumer relationship, and returns are mid-teens ROE with a weak year in the last five — not a wide-moat compounder.
name: Assurant, Inc.
one_liner: Specialty insurer with embedded partner distribution, moat 5/10 — B by numbers on a TTM base (15.4% weighted, IV@15 $292 vs $283) but the OCF base capitalizes float in a light-cat period, so softened to C at low confidence; it does not cleanly clear 15% until the bear case (12.5%) is covered.
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH insurer artifact (Andrew's standing rule, 2026-10-15; same treatment as PFG/HIG/ACGL/WRB): the OCF-based OE base capitalizes float/reserve growth — NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE is structural in 2023, 2024 and 2025 (FY2025 OCF $1,833,900,000 vs net income $872,700,000; maintenance OE $887,200,000 vs conservative OE $1,512,700,000) — and the TTM base ($31.23/sh) embeds a light-catastrophe H1 2026 (reportable cats $36.6M vs $186.8M in H1 2025), so tier-by-numbers B (weighted IRR 15.39%) overstates distributable owner's earnings; softened one notch to C, confidence low. The median-base preliminary run also printed Tier C (13.19%), and the bear case is C (12.45%).
